http.title: HTTP & hosters
http.description: Direct HTTP, DDownload cookies and the Premiumize API key share the same isolated client identity; signed components stay installable.

capture.title: Capture agent
capture.description: Clipboard, Click'n'Load, NZB file association and Windows hotfolders use the native agent.

usenet.title: Usenet
usenet.description: Server priorities and encrypted credentials are configurable; yEnc and safe post-processing building blocks are built in.

facts.web_ui_configured: Configured port · applied on next start

pairing.title: Pair native agent
pairing.description: The bearer secret is shown only once. Only its SHA-256 digest with the {scope} scope is persisted.
pairing.copy_hint: Copy now – it cannot be retrieved later
pairing.copied_description: The full command is in your clipboard.
pairing.extension_hint: Browser extension: use the raw token below in the extension options.
pairing.extension_steps: In the extension options set the server URL to {origin} and paste this token, then press “Test connection”. See extension/README.md for installation.
pairing.token_copied_description: The capture token is in your clipboard.

revoke.title: Remove capture connection
revoke.description: The agent “{label}” immediately loses access to LinkGrabber and NZB import.

export.title: Export settings
export.description: Download all server-side settings, categories, accounts and integrations as a versioned JSON bundle.
export.include_secrets_description: Credentials and cookies are protected with the passphrase and never written as plaintext.
export.passphrase_short: Use a passphrase with at least 8 characters.

import.title: Import settings
import.description: Restore or migrate a version 1 rDownloader settings bundle.
import.invalid_file: The selected file is not a valid rDownloader settings bundle.
import.passphrase_required: Enter the passphrase used to create this backup.
import.confirm_description: All settings, categories, accounts, proxies, Usenet servers, hotfolders and stream channels will be replaced. Pause active downloads first. Capture-agent hotfolders imported on another installation must be paired again.

mcp.title: API access & MCP
mcp.description: API tokens authenticate REST, the CLI, SABnzbd- and qBittorrent-compatible clients, and the MCP server at {endpoint}. Selectable areas replace blanket {scope} access; only the SHA-256 digest is persisted.
mcp.copy_hint: This API token is shown only once – store it safely in the intended client now.
mcp.token_hint: Raw token for clients that expect only the API key.
mcp.command_copied: The claude mcp add command is in your clipboard.
mcp.token_copied: The API token is in your clipboard.
mcp.header_hint: Clients that read the header from an environment variable (ChatGPT desktop): enter this complete value.
mcp.header_copied: The Authorization header is in your clipboard.
mcp.single_source_hint: Configure only one source for the Authorization header. If two are sent, only the first counts — a correct token in second place is never read.

revoke.title: Revoke API token
revoke.description: The client “{label}” immediately loses its API and MCP access.

edit.label: Change permissions
edit.hint: The token value stays the same: the client keeps working and reaches the new areas from its next request onwards. Removing everything is not possible here — revoke the token for that.
edit.empty: Choose at least one area, or revoke the token.

read.name: Read
read.description: Queue, progress, packages and system status. Grants nothing that changes anything.

intake.name: Add links
intake.description: Adding links, files and containers to the LinkGrabber. What a *arr instance or a browser extension needs.

queue.name: Control the queue
queue.description: Start, pause, retry, reorder and delete queued work.

config.name: Configuration
config.description: Categories, rules, schedules and service settings that carry no credential.

secrets.name: Stored credentials
secrets.description: Hoster accounts, proxy profiles, Usenet servers and the settings export. Nothing else grants this.

admin.name: Administration
admin.description: Plugins, service switches, updates and backups. Does not include stored credentials.

metrics.name: Metrics
metrics.description: Only the Prometheus route /api/v1/metrics. Reaches nothing else, not the queue and not MCP.

mcp.scopes_hint: Grant only what the client actually needs. Anything that acts can also read, so reading does not have to be added separately.
mcp.sensitive_warning: This token will be able to read stored credentials or administer the service. Nothing else grants either, so give it only to a client that genuinely needs it.

readiness.title: Is the setup finished?
readiness.complete: Everything the setup asks for is in place.
readiness.outstanding: One step is still open. | {count} steps are still open.

login.label: Administrator login
login.done: Set, or deliberately switched off for a trusted network.
login.missing: No password is set yet and the login is not switched off.

storage.label: Storage destination
storage.done: At least one destination is configured.
storage.missing: Downloads have nowhere to go until a destination exists.
storage.ephemeral: A destination is configured, but at least one is not on persistent storage.

category.label: Category
category.missing: Without a category nothing can be sorted into a folder.

wizard.label: Setup finished
wizard.missing: The setup was never finished; run it again from the sidebar.

sessions.title: Signed-in devices
sessions.description: Every open sign-in to this installation. If something here is not yours, end it and change the password.

revoke.title: End this session?
revoke.description_current: You will be signed out on this device and will have to sign in again.

revoke_others.title: Sign out everywhere else?
revoke_others.description: {count} other sessions will be ended. This one stays signed in.

proxy.title: Reverse proxy
proxy.description: If a proxy sits in front, rDownloader has to know about it. Otherwise every request counts as coming from the proxy, and the session cookie may not match the scheme the browser is actually using.
proxy.external_url_hint: Scheme, host and sub-path in one setting, so they cannot disagree. Leave empty when there is no proxy.
proxy.trusted_hint: One address or CIDR range per line. A forwarded client address is believed only from these; everything else counts as the caller itself.
proxy.cookie_hint: “Automatic” follows the scheme of the external URL and is right almost always.
proxy.warning_no_proxies: An external URL is set but no trusted proxy is. Every request will then look as though it came from the proxy: rate limiting and the session list show one address for everybody.
proxy.warning_no_url: Trusted proxies are set but no external URL is. The cookie then cannot be marked Secure automatically.

mfa.title: Two-factor sign-in
mfa.description: Optional. After the password, a code from an authenticator app is also required. The recovery codes are the only other way back in — there is nobody here to prove your identity to.

enrol.once: Visible only now. None of this can be retrieved once you leave the page.
enrol.scan: Scan this code with your authenticator app:
enrol.recovery: Recovery codes — keep these somewhere safe:
enrol.qr_alt: QR code for setting up the authenticator app
enrol.manual: Or enter the key by hand:

remove.title: Remove this second factor?
remove.description: “{label}” will no longer be able to answer a challenge.

regenerate.title: Issue new codes?
regenerate.description: The recovery codes you have now will stop working.

disable.label: Password
disable.hint: Switching it off takes the password, not a code. A lost device must not be final.

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.description: Sign in with your device instead of your password. Your authenticator checks a PIN or a fingerprint before it will sign, so one step covers both. The password keeps working — a passkey is another way in, not a replacement.
passkeys.unsupported: This browser cannot use passkeys here. They need a secure connection: either https, or reaching the service at localhost.
passkeys.failed: The passkey could not be set up.
passkeys.name_hint: So you know which device this is when you come to remove it.

remove.title: Remove this passkey?
remove.description: “{label}” will stop being able to sign in. Your password still works.

password.title: Administrator password
password.description: Replaces the password you sign in with. You need the current one for it. There is no recovery without the current password.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.sessions_hint: The change ends every session. This window stays signed in; every other device has to sign in again.
password.tokens_hint: API tokens keep working, because they do not hang off the password. Anyone who knew the old one could have issued themselves some, though: check the token list.

logs.title: Clear the service log?
logs.description: {count} log records will be removed for good. The audit log and the statistics stay, as do downloads, packages and settings.

audit.title: Clear the audit log?
audit.description: {count} audit records will be removed for good. The clearing itself becomes the first entry in the emptied log. The service log and the statistics stay, as do downloads, packages and settings.

stats.title: Clear the transfer statistics?
stats.description: {count} statistics rows will be removed for good, the all-time totals among them. The service log and the audit log stay, as do downloads, packages and settings.

notifications.title: Clear the notification history?
notifications.description: {count} finished deliveries will be removed from the history for good. Deliveries still queued or retrying stay, as do destinations, rules, the service log, the audit log and the statistics.

session_limits.title: How long a sign-in lasts
session_limits.description: A sign-in ends when it has not been used for this long or reaches its maximum lifetime, whichever comes first. A shorter setting ends older sign-ins at once.
session_limits.idle_description: Hours without a request before you have to sign in again. 1 to 720 (30 days).
session_limits.max_description: Hours from signing in after which it ends, even in the middle of work. 1 to 2160 (90 days).
